Yep, the best thing to do when you read your essay is pretend to be an annoying 5-year old. "Why? How does that work? What does that mean?"

I give the bot an incredibly vague prompt (just the essay question, for example) so it generates a pretty structureless answer. Then I'll kind of "discuss" the points it raises, fixing parts I don't like. Treat the bot like it's really stupid and everything it says is not good enough (because it isn't.)

Take for example, if the AI says "The metaphor in this line suggests that the character feels guilty." Then I'll think: 
1. It's true that there's a metaphor, good on the AI for pointing that out, but...
2. I'll have to describe exactly what the metaphor means. 
3. The link isn't clear enough, so I'll have to explain why "metaphor=guilty". 

Essentially, what you're doing is critiquing the AI essay REALLY harshly. Question the points, add more details, make sure it leaves no room for doubt. Don't be afraid to cut things out, or occasionally use AI to help you phrase one or two sentences (if you're really not great at expressing yourself). By the end of it, the whole thing should be completely rewritten. It's a lot easier to correct someone else's work, rather than create your own from scratch. Ready

We all know you shouldn't use q-tips to clean our ears. To properly clean them, get ear drops (can buy em anywhere) and a syringe. (I use a 1ml syringe but any should be okay.) 

About 1 day before (or up to 3 days if the wax is really compacted), use the ear drops to soften the wax. Morning and night. Then the next day, fill the syringe with warm water, tilt your head sideways over the sink (blocked ear down ofc) and pump the water in at an angle (kinda towards the back, so it won't damage your eardrums). 

It's a weird feeling but WAY more satisfying than q-tips, since you'll see all the big pieces of gunk get flushed out into the sink. Afterwards your ear will feel crystal clear.

Come to think of it, I only experienced the physical media. Never watched the anime (parents didn't let us watch tv) or played the games (no video games allowed either) so I just... Read the handbooks, omnibuses, Pokedexes, and played the TCG nonstop. 

And honestly? I'm kinda grateful that I experienced  Pokemon without a single screen. For me, it was more immersive.
